summary: Flame in Freefall is an interactive web dashboard that organizes NASA's microgravity combustion research so researchers and engineers can find, compare and understand it. It covers 26 investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, grouped into fire prevention, detection and suppression. Users can compare investigations side by side, rank them by relevance to a spacecraft, Moon base or spacesuit, and see where the research falls short, such as the lack of Moon and Mars gravity data. As humans return to the Moon and head to Mars, safer habitats depend on understanding fire in space, and this tool makes decades of scattered research easier to use.
details: The dashboard has five tabs: Explore (search and filter all 26 investigations), Compare (side by side), Rank (a scored list for three environments, with a visible formula), Gaps, and Method. We grouped the investigations into prevention (Saffire, BASS, BASS-II, BRE), detection (SAME, SAME-R, DAFT) and suppression (FLEX, FLEX-2), plus fundamental flame science and ground studies that reuse flight data for modeling. The Gaps tab shows that PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data, that solid-material tests may not cover the 30%+ oxygen expected in Moon habitats (flagged for verification), and that NASA's standard upward-burn test may not be conservative in space. It also links the research to Earth applications such as fire detectors, firefighter air tanks and protective clothing. This is a prototype: most oxygen, pressure and airflow values are not yet extracted, so the ranking mainly reflects investigation type. Built as a single HTML/JavaScript web page.
dataRefs: A Researcher's Guide to Combustion Science
